title: Navimower 0.4.5-beta41

## Private-cloud token recovery and Home Assistant startup cleanup

This beta fixes a private-cloud authentication edge case observed in live Home Assistant logs and removes two Home Assistant runtime warnings.

### Recover vendor `401903: token expired`

The private cloud can report business code `401903` when the stored app-cloud access token expires. Navimower now treats `401903` as an authentication/session error, including when the vendor serializes the code as a string.

The existing recovery path is then used as intended:

1. refresh the Passport token;
2. re-login the mower-cloud session;
3. retry the failed endpoint once.

If the refresh itself is no longer valid, the failure is promoted to a private-cloud authentication error so Home Assistant can start the existing private reauthentication flow instead of repeatedly polling every endpoint with an expired token.

Normal endpoint failures still retain last-good data. Private endpoint warning/recovery messages now also include a masked mower serial so multi-mower installations can identify which config entry is affected without logging the full serial number.

### Keep `mower_sdk` imports off the event loop

GitHub issue #377 showed Home Assistant detecting a blocking `listdir` call while `mower_sdk` was imported from MQTT startup. Importing that dependency can invoke Python package metadata discovery, which may touch the filesystem.

The Smart Home `MowerAPI` / `NavimowSDK` imports used by MQTT startup now run through Home Assistant's executor. The same protection is applied to the OAuth/config-flow validation import so the blocking work cannot move to reauthentication or setup.

This changes only where the Python dependency is loaded; MQTT, OAuth and mower command semantics are unchanged.

### Home Assistant device-registry compatibility

Map API frontend metadata now resolves the mower device with `async_get_device_by_identifier` instead of the deprecated `async_get_device` lookup. This removes the Home Assistant deprecation warning and keeps the integration aligned with the API required before Home Assistant 2027.8.

No Navimower Map Card update or configuration migration is required for this beta.
